biological.citation: Chemical perturbations reveal that RUVBL2 regulates the circadian phase in mammals. (PMID: 32376767)
biological.summary: RUVBL2 interacts with core clock proteins on chromatin to regulate circadian phase in human cells and mice. Pharmacological perturbation of RUVBL2 with cordycepin caused a rapid-onset 12-hour clock phase-shift phenotype, and biochemical assays showed cordycepin treatment caused disassembly of the RUVBL2-BMAL1 interaction and the circadian super-complex at E-box chromatin loci (PER1, PER2, DBP, NR1D1). Cordycepin penetrated the blood-brain barrier and facilitated reduced jet-lag recovery duration in mice.

biological.citation: The P-loop NTPase RUVBL2 is a conserved clock component across eukaryotes. (PMID: 40140583)
biological.summary: RUVBL2 is identified as a conserved core circadian clock component across eukaryotes, influencing circadian period through its remarkably slow ATPase activity (~13 ATP molecules/day). RUVBL2 variants delivered by AAV to the murine suprachiasmatic nucleus produced arrhythmic, short-period, and long-period locomotor activity phenotypes. Physical interactions between RUVBL2 orthologues and core clock proteins were demonstrated in humans, Drosophila, and Neurospora, with consistent circadian phenotypes across species.

biological.citation: Ruvbl2 Suppresses Cardiomyocyte Proliferation During Zebrafish Heart Development and Regeneration. (PMID: 35178388)
biological.summary: In zebrafish, loss-of-function ruvbl2 mutants (both the lik allele and a null deletion allele) display ventricular hyperplasia due to cardiomyocyte hyperproliferation, demonstrating that Ruvbl2 suppresses cardiomyocyte proliferation. Constitutive myocardial overexpression of Ruvbl2 was sufficient to suppress cardiomyocyte proliferation in control hearts and rescue hyperproliferation in ruvbl2 null mutants. Heat-shock-inducible overexpression of Ruvbl2 during heart regeneration suppressed cardiomyocyte proliferation and led to scarring.

biological.citation: Targeting MYC effector functions in pancreatic cancer by inhibiting the ATPase RUVBL1/2. (PMID: 38821858)
biological.summary: RUVBL1 and RUVBL2 ranked first among MYC binding partners essential for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) tumor growth both in vitro and in vivo in mouse models. Degradation of RUVBL1 via the auxin-degron system arrested cultured PDAC cells but not untransformed cells, and caused complete tumor regression in mice preceded by immune cell infiltration. Mechanistically, RUVBL1/2 were required for MYC to establish oncogenic and immunoevasive gene expression programs.

biological.citation: RUVBL1/2 Blockade Targets YTHDF1 Activity to Suppress m6A-Dependent Oncogenic Translation and Colorectal Tumorigenesis. (PMID: 38900944)
biological.summary: A CRISPR/Cas9 screen identified RUVBL1 and RUVBL2 as synthetic lethal targets in YTHDF1-high colorectal cancer cells. RUVBL1/2 were overexpressed in primary colorectal cancer samples and predicted poor prognosis. Mechanistically, YTHDF1 bound m6A-modified RUVBL1/2 mRNA to promote their translation, while RUVBL1/2 reciprocally interacted with YTHDF1 at 40S translation initiation complexes to drive oncogenic translation via MAPK, RAS, and PI3K-AKT signaling.

biological.citation: Mycobacterium tuberculosis suppresses host DNA repair to boost its intracellular survival. (PMID: 37848028)
biological.summary: Mycobacterium tuberculosis urease C (UreC) interacts with RUVBL2 and impedes formation of the RUVBL1-RUVBL2-RAD51 DNA repair complex in macrophages. This suppression of DNA repair increases micronuclei abundance, triggering the cGAS/STING pathway and IFN-β production, which upregulates SR-A1 to form lipid droplets that facilitate Mtb replication. Thus, RUVBL2 is a component of a host DNA repair complex targeted by a bacterial virulence factor.

biological.citation: RuvBL1/2 reduce toxic dipeptide repeat protein burden in multiple models of C9orf72-ALS/FTD. (PMID: 39638345)
biological.summary: C9ALS/FTD patients show reduced expression of RuvBL1 and RuvBL2 compared to controls. Overexpression of RuvBL2 (more potently than RuvBL1) reduced C9orf72-associated dipeptide repeat proteins in cell lines, primary neurons from C9-500 transgenic mice, and patient-derived iPSC motor neurons. In a Drosophila model, RuvBL2 overexpression and consequent DPR reduction rescued DPR-related motor phenotypes.

biological.citation: PPARγ enhanced Adiponectin polymerization and trafficking by promoting RUVBL2 expression during adipogenic differentiation. (PMID: 32877748)
biological.summary: RUVBL2 expression is concurrently upregulated with PPARγ and Adiponectin during days 5-7 of 3T3-L1 adipogenic differentiation. PPARγ directly binds the RUVBL2 promoter at a binding motif at -804/-781 bp to transcriptionally activate RUVBL2 expression, as confirmed by ChIP assay and promoter deletion/mutation analysis. RUVBL2 overexpression enhanced Adiponectin polymerization and secretion, while RUVBL2 knockdown reduced Adiponectin secretion.

biological.citation: Multilevel regulation of RUVBL2 expression predicts poor prognosis in hepatocellular carcinoma. (PMID: 31572066)
biological.summary: RUVBL2 is overexpressed in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) due to promoter hypomethylation, copy number gain, MYC amplification, and CTNNB1 mutation. High RUVBL2 protein expression independently predicted worse overall survival (HR ~2.03) and recurrence-free survival (HR ~1.71) in 153 HCC patients. RUVBL2 overexpression promoted carcinogenesis through the HSP90-CDC37, AKT, and ERK/MAPK signaling pathways.
biological.sample_size: 153 HCC patients; 371 TCGA liver cancer patients

biological.citation: Regulation of RUVBL1-RUVBL2 AAA-ATPases by the nonsense-mediated mRNA decay factor DHX34, as evidenced by Cryo-EM. (PMID: 33205750)
biological.summary: The NMD RNA helicase DHX34 directly interacts with the RUVBL1-RUVBL2 complex both in vitro and in cells. Cryo-EM revealed that DHX34 induces extensive conformational changes specifically in the N-termini of RUVBL2 subunits, stabilizing a nucleotide-free conformation that downregulates ATP hydrolysis of the complex. ATPase-deficient mutant analysis confirmed DHX34 acts exclusively on RUVBL2 subunits, coupling RUVBL1-RUVBL2 ATPase activity to NMD initiation.
